title: Analysis of reactive astrogliosis in mouse brain using in situ hybridization combined with immunohistochemistry
protocol: Place mouse in isoflurane chamber to anesthetize the animal.
Administer ketamine/xylazine mixture via intraperitoneal injection (up to 80 mg/kg body weight ketamine and 10 mg/kg body weight xylazine).
Determine depth of anesthesia using toe pinch response method.
Make a 5-6 cm lateral incision through integument and abdominal wall just beneath rib cage.
Continue diaphragm incision along entire length of rib cage to expose pleural cavity.
Insert 30-gauge needle into posterior end of left ventricle carefully.
Make an incision to the animal's right atrium using iris scissors to create as large an outlet as possible without damaging descending aorta.
Open and attach outlet port to needle base for perfusion setup.
Pump up the manometer bulb to a pressure of 80 mm Hg.
Perfuse mouse with saline solution for 10 min.
Switch stopcock to allow flow of formalin solution at same rate as saline.
Perfuse mouse with 4% PFA solution for 10–15 min.
Cut posterior from the ears and separate the mouse head using surgical scissors.
Make a caudal midline incision in the skin, working rostrally to remove skin from skull.
Cut through top of skull along midline between eyes with Iris scissors.
Remove parietal and frontal bone plates by tilting one side each time and snapping off with tweezers.
Tilt brain upward anteriorly with tweezers and cut optic nerves and cranial nerves.
Gently lift the brain out of the skull.
Place the removed brain in a vial containing fixative fluid at least 10× the volume of the brain.
Swirl the vial occasionally to ensure proper fixation.
Fix biopsies (3×3 mm) immediately in freshly prepared 4% (w/v) PFA/PBS for 12–18 h.
Label plastic molds for frozen block preparation with a permanent marker.
Cover the bottom of the mold with NEG50 or OCT freezing compound.
Prechill acetone in a Petri dish placed on dry ice pellets.
Place the prechilled Petri dish on top of dry ice inside a Styrofoam box.
Work in a fume hood.
Put a minimal amount of acetone into a petri dish so the bottom is covered.
Carefully add dry ice pellets to the dish with acetone, leaving enough room for the mold.
Wait until the pellets stop bubbling vigorously and the "slurry" is ready.
Add more dry ice pellets as needed to maintain temperature.
Fill the mold and orient the tissue.
Place the filled mold in the cold acetone to freeze it.
Remove the brain from the 30% sucrose solution.
Use forceps to keep the brain in an upright position.
Hold a corner of the brain on a Kimwipe to release excess liquid.
Place the brain on the empty dish on ice.
Cut the bottom part of the brain to keep it level, if required.
Place the brain into molds filled with NEG50.
Mix the brain gently with NEG50.
Orient the brain as required for efficient sectioning.
Cover the tissue with NEG50 and fill up the mold.
Freeze quickly by placing the mold on petri dish with acetone on dry ice.
Allow it to stand on dry ice until the block is fully white and solid.
Dry the bottom of the mold with a paper towel.
Wrap the mold with aluminum foil or parafilm and label it.
Store at −20°C for short storage (5 days or less) or −80°C for long-term storage.
Thaw-mount the sections onto Superfrost-coated positive charged histological slides.
Dry the slides for approximately 10 minutes on a slide warmer at 37°C.
Post-fix sections for 5 minutes with sterile 4% PFA in PBS.
Wash sections with sterile PBS, twice for 5 minutes each time.
Permeabilize sections for 2 minutes with 1 μg/mL RNase-free Proteinase K in PBS.
Wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes.
Re-fix sections for 5 minutes with 4% PFA in PBS.
Wash sections with PBS three times, each time for 5 minutes.
Incubate sections with 70% EtOH for 5 minutes.
Incubate sections with 95% EtOH for 2 minutes.
Air dry sections in open humid chambers until dry.
Prepare hybridization probe in Hybridization Solution at 80°C for 3 minutes.
Pipette 250–300 μL of probe per slide and cover with a parafilm coverslip.
Incubate slides in a humid chamber overnight at 65°C.
Turn on water baths at 37°C and 65°C the next day.
Remove coverslips by immersing slides in 5× SSC.
Wash sections with high-stringency wash buffer for 30 minutes at 65°C.
Incubate sections with RNase buffer containing 20 μg/mL RNase A for 30 minutes at 37°C to digest unbound RNA probe.
Wash sections with RNase buffer three times, each time for 10 minutes at 37°C.
Wash sections with RNase buffer for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Heat sections in a water bath at 65°C for 2 × 20 minutes.
Wash sections in a water bath at 37°C with 2× SSC for 15 minutes.
Wash sections in a water bath at 37°C with 0.1× SSC for 15 minutes.
Wash the sections with PBT (PBS + 0.1% Tween 20) at 20°C–22°C for 15 minutes.
Cover slides with 250–300 μL/slide blocking solution (10% NGS in PBT with 0.5 mg/mL Levamisol) in a humid chamber for 120 minutes.
Wash the slides with PBT at 20°C–22°C, 4 × 5 minutes each time.
Cover the slides with 250–300 μL/slide anti-DIG antibody (1:2,500 diluted in 10% NGS in PBT) in a humid chamber overnight at 4°C for 12–18 hours.
Decant the anti-DIG antibody and wash the slides with PBT in a coplin jar 6 × over 5 hours.
Wash sections with NTMT buffer, 2 × 10 minutes each time.
Cover each sample slide with approximately 300 μL of BM-Purple exposure solution for 30 minutes to 16 hours in a dark humid chamber until desired color development is achieved.
Stop the color reaction by incubating the slides in PBS, 2 × 5 minutes each time.
Wash sections in PBS for 5 min.
Wash sections with 0.3% H2O2 in PBS to inhibit endogenous peroxidase activity for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 5 min each time.
Dry back of slide with tissue paper and add ∼325 μL anti-GFAP antibody (1:1,000) in blocking buffer and incubate for 12–18 h in humid chamber at 20°C–22°C.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 5 min each time.
Add ∼325 μL biotinylated secondary antibody (1:500) in blocking buffer and incubate 2 h in humid chamber.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 5 min each time.
Incubate the sections in avidin and biotinylated horseradish peroxidase macromolecular complex (ABC reagent), 10 μL/mL each of reagents A and B and 10% Triton X-100 in 1 mL PBS for 1 h.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 5 min each time.
Add approximately 300 μL DAB per slide.
Observe color development through a microscope.
Stop reaction when desired color is obtained.
Mount slides with appropriately sized coverslip and Vectashield antifade mounting medium.
Select three consecutive visual fields under a 20× objective for astrocyte density calculation.
Count the number of astrocytes using Image J Cell Counter plugin.
